[2025 summer phd math-stat — problem 4]

Part IV. Observe i.i.d. $(X_i, Y_i)$ with $\mathbb{E}(Y \mid X) = X^T\beta^*$; split $X = (Z, W^T)^T$, $\beta^* = (\theta^*, \alpha^{*T})^T$ with $Z, \theta^*$ scalar and $Z$ binary. Let $\hat\beta$ be the Lasso-penalized least squares estimator, and $\hat\gamma$ the Lasso-penalized logistic-regression estimator of $Z$ on $W$. Consider the debiased estimator $\tilde\theta = \frac{(Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\hat\gamma))^T(Y - W\hat\alpha)/n}{(Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\hat\gamma))^T Z/n}$, with $\mathrm{expit}(u) = e^u/(1 + e^u)$. The goal is the asymptotic expansion $\tilde\theta - \theta^* = \frac{(Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\bar\gamma))^T(Y - Z\theta^* - W\alpha^*)/n}{(Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\bar\gamma))^T Z/n} + o_p(n^{-1/2})$, reducing to establishing equation (4) in the exam.
1) Show $|(Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\hat\gamma))^T(Y - Z\theta^* - W\hat\alpha)/n - (Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\bar\gamma))^T(Y - Z\theta^* - W\alpha^*)/n| \le \underbrace{|(Z - \mathrm{expit}(W\hat\gamma))^T W(\hat\alpha - \alpha^*)/n|}_{I} + \underbrace{|(\mathrm{expit}(W\hat\gamma) - \mathrm{expit}(W\bar\gamma))^T(Y - Z\theta^* - W\alpha^*)/n|}_{II}$.
2) Show, under suitable conditions, $I = O_p(1)(|S_{\beta^*}| + |S_{\bar\gamma}|)\frac{\log(n\vee p)}{n}$. State the conditions explicitly (you may use standard $\hat\beta, \hat\gamma$ rate properties).
3) Show that for any $u, \tilde u \in \mathbb{R}$: $|\mathrm{expit}_2(u) - \mathrm{expit}_2(\tilde u)| \le \mathrm{expit}_2(\tilde u)|u - \tilde u|$ and $|\mathrm{expit}(u) - \mathrm{expit}(\tilde u) - \mathrm{expit}_2(\tilde u)(u - \tilde u)| \le \mathrm{expit}_2(\tilde u)(u - \tilde u)^2$, where $\mathrm{expit}_2(u) = \mathrm{expit}(u)(1 - \mathrm{expit}(u))$.
4) Assume $Y - Z\theta^* - W^T\alpha^*$ is bounded by $B_0$ a.s. Show under suitable (explicitly stated) conditions that $II = O_p(1)(|S_{\beta^*}| + |S_{\bar\gamma}|)\frac{\log(n\vee p)}{n}$. (Combining 1,2,4 gives (4) when $(|S_{\beta^*}| + |S_{\bar\gamma}|)\frac{\log(n\vee p)}{\sqrt n} = o(1)$.)

response.text:
Let

\[
\varepsilon_i:=Y_i-Z_i\theta^*-W_i^T\alpha^*,\qquad 
m(u):=\operatorname{expit}(u),\qquad 
g(u):=m(u)\{1-m(u)\}.
\]

Write \(m_{\hat\gamma,i}=m(W_i^T\hat\gamma)\), \(m_{\bar\gamma,i}=m(W_i^T\bar\gamma)\), and let \(L_n:=\log(n\vee p)\). Also write \(s_\beta:=|S_{\beta^*}|\), \(s_\gamma:=|S_{\bar\gamma}|\).

A recurring target rate is

\[
(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{n}=o(n^{-1/2})
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{\sqrt n}\to 0.
\]

---

## 1) Algebraic decomposition

We have

\[
Y-Z\theta^*-W\hat\alpha
=
\varepsilon-W(\hat\alpha-\alpha^*).
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^T(Y-Z\theta^*-W\hat\alpha)}{n}
-\frac{(Z-m_{\bar\gamma})^T(Y-Z\theta^*-W\alpha^*)}{n} \\
&=
\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^T\{\varepsilon-W(\hat\alpha-\alpha^*)\}}{n}
-\frac{(Z-m_{\bar\gamma})^T\varepsilon}{n} \\
&=
-\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^TW(\hat\alpha-\alpha^*)}{n}
+\frac{(m_{\bar\gamma}-m_{\hat\gamma})^T\varepsilon}{n}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Taking absolute values and applying the triangle inequality gives

\[
\begin{aligned}
&\left|
\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^T(Y-Z\theta^*-W\hat\alpha)}{n}
-\frac{(Z-m_{\bar\gamma})^T(Y-Z\theta^*-W\alpha^*)}{n}
\right| \\
&\le 
\left|\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^TW(\hat\alpha-\alpha^*)}{n}\right|
+
\left|\frac{(m_{\hat\gamma}-m_{\bar\gamma})^T\varepsilon}{n}\right| \\
&=: I+II.
\end{aligned}
\]

This proves the desired inequality.

---

## 2) Bound for \(I\)

Assume the logistic Lasso estimator \(\hat\gamma\) is defined by

\[
\hat\gamma
\in \arg\min_\gamma
\left\{
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[\log\{1+\exp(W_i^T\gamma)\}-Z_iW_i^T\gamma\right]
+\lambda_\gamma \|\gamma\|_1
\right\},
\]

with

\[
\lambda_\gamma \asymp \sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}.
\]

By the KKT conditions for logistic Lasso,

\[
\left\|
\frac1n W^T\{Z-m(W\hat\gamma)\}
\right\|_\infty
\le \lambda_\gamma .
\]

Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
I
&=
\left|
\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^TW(\hat\alpha-\alpha^*)}{n}
\right| \\
&\le
\left\|
\frac1n W^T(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})
\right\|_\infty
\|\hat\alpha-\alpha^*\|_1 \\
&\le
\lambda_\gamma \|\hat\alpha-\alpha^*\|_1.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now assume the usual Lasso oracle rate for \(\hat\beta=(\hat\theta,\hat\alpha^T)^T\):

\[
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
=
O_p\left(s_\beta\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right),
\]

which holds, for example, under a restricted eigenvalue/compatibility condition on the design \(X\), sub-Gaussian or bounded covariates, and \(\lambda_\beta\asymp \sqrt{L_n/n}\). Then

\[
\|\hat\alpha-\alpha^*\|_1
\le
\|\hat\beta-\beta^*\|_1
=
O_p\left(s_\beta\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
I
\le
\lambda_\gamma \|\hat\alpha-\alpha^*\|_1
=
O_p\left(\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right)
O_p\left(s_\beta\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right)
=
O_p\left(s_\beta\frac{L_n}{n}\right).
\]

Since \(s_\beta\le s_\beta+s_\gamma\),

\[
I
=
O_p(1)(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{n}.
\]

---

## 3) Logistic derivative inequalities

The two inequalities stated in the question are **not true globally as written**.

Indeed, take \(u=0\) and \(\tilde u=10\). Then

\[
g(0)=\frac14,\qquad 
g(10)=\frac{e^{10}}{(1+e^{10})^2}\approx 4.54\times 10^{-5}.
\]

The claimed inequality

\[
|g(u)-g(\tilde u)|
\le
g(\tilde u)|u-\tilde u|
\]

would give

\[
0.25 \lesssim 4.54\times 10^{-4},
\]

which is false. The second claimed inequality also fails for the same choice.

The correct standard inequalities are the following. Since

\[
g(u)=m(u)\{1-m(u)\}
\]

and

\[
g'(u)=g(u)\{1-2m(u)\},
\]

we have

\[
|g'(u)|\le g(u).
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\left|\frac{d}{du}\log g(u)\right|
=
|1-2m(u)|
\le 1.
\]

Therefore, for \(d=u-\tilde u\),

\[
g(\tilde u+s)\le e^{|s|}g(\tilde u),
\qquad 0\le |s|\le |d|.
\]

Hence

\[
\begin{aligned}
|g(u)-g(\tilde u)|
&=
\left|\int_0^d g'(\tilde u+s)\,ds\right| \\
&\le
\int_0^{|d|} g(\tilde u+s)\,ds \\
&\le
g(\tilde u)\int_0^{|d|} e^s\,ds \\
&=
g(\tilde u)(e^{|d|}-1) \\
&\le
e^{|d|}g(\tilde u)|d|.
\end{aligned}
\]

Similarly,

\[
\begin{aligned}
&|m(u)-m(\tilde u)-g(\tilde u)(u-\tilde u)| \\
&=
\left|
\int_0^d \{g(\tilde u+s)-g(\tilde u)\}\,ds
\right| \\
&\le
\int_0^{|d|}
g(\tilde u)(e^s-1)\,ds \\
&=
g(\tilde u)(e^{|d|}-1-|d|) \\
&\le
\frac12 e^{|d|}g(\tilde u)d^2.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus, on events where \(|u-\tilde u|\le C\), the claimed bounds hold up to a harmless multiplicative constant depending only on \(C\). This is the version needed for the \(O_p\)-bound in part 4.

---

## 4) Bound for \(II\)

Assume now that

\[
|\varepsilon_i|
=
|Y_i-Z_i\theta^*-W_i^T\alpha^*|
\le B_0
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

Let

\[
\delta:=\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma,
\qquad 
d_i:=W_i^T\delta,
\qquad 
\bar g_i:=g(W_i^T\bar\gamma).
\]

Then

\[
m(W_i^T\hat\gamma)-m(W_i^T\bar\gamma)
=
\bar g_i d_i+r_i,
\]

where, using the corrected logistic Taylor bound from part 3,

\[
|r_i|
\le
C_n \bar g_i d_i^2,
\]

with

\[
C_n:=\frac12\exp\left(\max_{1\le i\le n}|W_i^T(\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma)|\right).
\]

Assume the standard logistic Lasso rates

\[
\|\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma\|_1
=
O_p\left(s_\gamma\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right),
\]

and

\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\bar g_i\{W_i^T(\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma)\}^2
=
O_p\left(s_\gamma\frac{L_n}{n}\right).
\]

Also assume the local boundedness condition

\[
\max_{1\le i\le n}|W_i^T(\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma)|=O_p(1),
\]

so that \(C_n=O_p(1)\). This condition follows, for example, if \(\max_{i,j}|W_{ij}|\le K\) and

\[
s_\gamma\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}=O(1).
\]

Now decompose \(II\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
II
&=
\left|
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\{m(W_i^T\hat\gamma)-m(W_i^T\bar\gamma)\}\varepsilon_i
\right| \\
&\le
\left|
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\bar g_i W_i^T(\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma)\varepsilon_i
\right|
+
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n |r_i||\varepsilon_i| \\
&=: II_1+II_2.
\end{aligned}
\]

For \(II_1\),

\[
II_1
=
\left|
\delta^T
\left\{
\frac1n W^T D_{\bar\gamma}\varepsilon
\right\}
\right|,
\]

where

\[
D_{\bar\gamma}:=\operatorname{diag}(\bar g_1,\dots,\bar g_n).
\]

Thus

\[
II_1
\le
\|\delta\|_1
\left\|
\frac1n W^TD_{\bar\gamma}\varepsilon
\right\|_\infty.
\]

Because

\[
\mathbb E(\varepsilon\mid Z,W)=0,
\]

we have

\[
\mathbb E\{W_j\bar g(W)\varepsilon\}=0.
\]

Under bounded or sub-Gaussian covariates and bounded \(\varepsilon\), a union bound plus Bernstein/Hoeffding gives

\[
\left\|
\frac1n W^TD_{\bar\gamma}\varepsilon
\right\|_\infty
=
O_p\left(\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right).
\]

Therefore

\[
II_1
=
O_p\left(s_\gamma\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right)
O_p\left(\sqrt{\frac{L_n}{n}}\right)
=
O_p\left(s_\gamma\frac{L_n}{n}\right).
\]

For \(II_2\), using \(|\varepsilon_i|\le B_0\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
II_2
&\le
B_0 C_n
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\bar g_i\{W_i^T(\hat\gamma-\bar\gamma)\}^2 \\
&=
O_p(1)
O_p\left(s_\gamma\frac{L_n}{n}\right) \\
&=
O_p\left(s_\gamma\frac{L_n}{n}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Combining the two pieces,

\[
II
=
O_p\left(s_\gamma\frac{L_n}{n}\right).
\]

Since \(s_\gamma\le s_\beta+s_\gamma\),

\[
II
=
O_p(1)(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{n}.
\]

---

Combining parts 1, 2, and 4,

\[
\left|
\frac{(Z-m_{\hat\gamma})^T(Y-Z\theta^*-W\hat\alpha)}{n}
-
\frac{(Z-m_{\bar\gamma})^T(Y-Z\theta^*-W\alpha^*)}{n}
\right|
=
O_p(1)(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{n}.
\]

Hence, if

\[
(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{\sqrt n}\to 0,
\]

then the difference is \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\), which is the desired equation (4).

O_p(1)(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{n}.
\]

Hence, if

\[
(s_\beta+s_\gamma)\frac{L_n}{\sqrt n}\to 0,
\]

then the difference is \(o_p(n^{-1/2})\), which is the desired equation (4).
